questions.q: Which five classes make up the chapter's workload label taxonomy?
options: OLTP, OLAP, HTAP, ETL, SYSTEM
OLTP_POINT, OLTP_MODERATE, ANALYTICAL, BATCH_ETL, MAINTENANCE
READ, WRITE, MIXED, IDLE, LOCKED
FAST, MEDIUM, SLOW, TINY, LARGE
questions.explain: The five-class taxonomy is precise enough to guide action (routing, resource pools, plan enforcement) yet stable enough to avoid thrashing.

questions.q: What happens when the classifier's confidence falls below 0.65?
options: The query is assigned OLTP_MODERATE as a safe default with confidence 0.0 and published to a human review queue for manual labeling
The model retrains itself immediately
The query is killed to protect the system
It is classified as ANALYTICAL by default
questions.explain: Below 0.65, misclassifications cause more harm than the safe default of OLTP_MODERATE, and the query feeds the weekly retraining loop via human labels.

questions.q: A reclassification is committed to the routing table only after:
options: One scoring interval above the threshold
A DBA approves it in Slack
The model is retrained
The new classification persists for 3 consecutive scoring intervals (about 3 minutes at the 60-second default cadence)
questions.explain: The hysteresis filter prevents thrashing on transient skew: three consecutive intervals of the new class are required before routing changes are applied.

questions.q: What Population Stability Index value triggers model retraining in the drift detector?
options: Any nonzero PSI
PSI > 0.2
PSI > 0.9
questions.explain: PSI under 0.1 is no drift, 0.1-0.2 is monitor, and above 0.2 on any feature fires the retraining pipeline (also when the KS test rejects at 1%).

questions.q: What plan enforcement policy does the chapter prescribe for OLTP_POINT queries?
options: Freeze the plan on first stable execution; force via SQL Server plan guide or Query Store plan forcing
No plan locking; allow the optimizer full freedom
Lock to the validated plan for each ETL step only
Auto-test new plans and merely alert on change
questions.explain: OLTP_POINT queries must never suddenly acquire a parallel plan or hash join they didn't have — plan changes there are almost always regressions, so the plan is frozen and forced.
